PullRequest.Title: sessions: Add depth to Codicon backgrounds
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Give the opt-in Codicons background in the Agents Window a calmer sense of depth without adding motion:

- Group icons into deterministic far, middle, and near layers with distinct contrast and softness.
- Use supported compact glyphs for the distant layer and base-size glyphs for the other layers, without scale transforms.
- Quiet the center behind the composer while preserving the existing grid and glyph placement.
- Keep the wallpaper static during scrolling, pointer input, and idle time, and skip unchanged opacity assignments.
- Preserve sticky-background continuity, image backgrounds, and the keyboard-accessible Celebrate action. High-contrast themes continue to omit the wallpaper and Celebrate control.

No new settings, dependency changes, or lockfile changes.

## Validation

- Client transpilation, `npm run typecheck-client`, and module-layer checks passed.
- 44 focused background, replica, confetti, and compact-glyph tests passed.
- Opacity regressions verify zero assignments for unchanged refreshes and scrolling, while resizing within the same grid still updates the fade.
- Targeted TypeScript/CSS lint and normal pre-commit hygiene passed.
- 52 affected fixtures passed render/dispose checks; Dark, Light, DarkHighContrast, and LightHighContrast screenshots passed stability and visual checks.
- 44 CI Playwright fixture tests passed, and all 3,189 fixtures rendered without errors.
- Updated the eight affected screenshot baselines and added both high-contrast baselines from CI; the baseline generator passes.

## Manual Testing

1. Select **Codicons** as the Agents Window chat background.
2. Inspect a new session and an existing conversation in dark and light themes.
3. Scroll the conversation and move the pointer: the background should remain still and align with the sticky header.
4. Confirm the **Celebrate** action remains keyboard-accessible in normal themes.
5. Switch to each high-contrast theme: neither the wallpaper nor the Celebrate control should appear.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The resize-observer call path, same-grid style mutation, realistic icon count, and replica multiplication are directly established by production code and the added tests. Exact frame loss varies by viewport, GPU, and number of visible sessions, which is reflected in medium severity rather than uncertainty about the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Inline style mutations and repaint/raster work for the Codicon DOM, including the newly filtered far-depth surface
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On every size change, work grows with the effective grid cardinality, about ceil(width/80) × ceil(height/80) cells, and is repeated by the source renderer plus each visible chat's sticky-background replica.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Continuous Agents-window or session-grid resizing can repeatedly invalidate most of the wallpaper and drop frames, with the cost amplified for large windows and multiple visible sessions.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A resize within the same 80px grid dimensions scanned the existing cells but did not mutate their opacity; existing glyphs were repainted only when cells were added or removed at a grid boundary.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The viewport-relative center fade changes `layout.opacity` whenever width or height changes, and this added branch writes a new inline opacity to every affected existing icon. The far half of the grid now also sits under a full-layer blur, so those writes invalidate its filtered raster.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 261-272 add viewport-normalized opacity and the inline `existingCell.icon.style.opacity` mutation; before this diff opacity was assigned only when a cell was created.
Findings.Title: Keep the center fade out of per-glyph resize updates
Findings.Impact: Dragging the Agents window or its session-grid sizing UI now performs repeated per-glyph style updates and wallpaper repaints on the resize critical path. At the test's 960×800 size there are already 109 icons, and the count grows by viewport area; every visible chat can also own a full-size replica renderer.
Findings.Evidence: `SessionsChatBackgroundRenderer` observes its host with `DisposableResizeObserver` and immediately schedules `renderCodicons`; lines 261-272 derive opacity from exact viewport dimensions and write it when changed. The added test explicitly requires `resizeWrites > 0` for a one-pixel same-grid resize, while the adjacent stability test establishes 109 icons at 960×800. `SessionsChatBackgroundReplica` creates another renderer sized to the full source, and `SessionsPart.updateVisibleSessions` creates one chat view per visible session, so the same resize work is duplicated across replicas.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve each icon's stable random opacity and express the viewport-relative center attenuation once on the shared Codicon container (for example with a radial mask/gradient), or otherwise update one shared visual property per resize instead of every icon; keep replica alignment and the current fade semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch to an Agents window using the Codicons background
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `SessionsPart.createContentArea` synchronously calls `setBackground`, which builds the viewport-sized glyph grid before the wallpaper is ready; each chat sticky replica builds the same grid when its sticky node is laid out.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is roughly 8/9 × ceil(viewport width / 80) × ceil(viewport height / 80) glyphs for the source and again for each visible session's replica; the focused test establishes 109 glyphs at 960×800.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderers execute independently on the UI thread. Initial source and replica creation is not protected by a shared limiter, but the diff only adds three lightweight containers and local compact-icon lookups on this path, so startup cost alone is not a separately reportable regression.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each renderer retains cells in a map and reuses them while the grid dimensions remain stable. Compact-icon registry lookups occur only for newly created far cells; there is no network or persistent cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor, `setBackground`, grid calculation, and replica ownership were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large/high-DPI viewport and visible-session counts vary, but the DOM cardinality and synchronous initialization path are concrete.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for initial creation: the additional depth containers and local lookups do not independently establish meaningful startup degradation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Continuously resize the Agents window or its multi-session grid with the Codicons background enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ResizeObserver schedules `renderCodicons` on the UI thread; the viewport-relative fade then updates affected icon styles before the next paint. Source resize also relays dimensions to each sticky replica, whose own renderer repeats the work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with viewport-area grid cells and with one source plus the number of visible chat replicas. A same-grid one-pixel resize now mutates opacity despite creating or deleting no cells.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each renderer has a zero-delay `RunOnceScheduler`, which coalesces bursts per renderer but not across renderers; during continuous resize each source/replica scheduler can run once per delivered resize cycle on the same UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cell objects are warm and reused, but exact numeric opacity changes defeat the style-write cache for central cells on every distinct width or height. Unchanged refreshes correctly avoid writes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: production observers and replica flow plus added tests directly prove same-grid opacity writes and realistic cell count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact repaint duration and dropped-frame prevalence depend on GPU, viewport size, and visible-session count; the style mutation, filtered-layer invalidation, and multiplicative cardinality are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium rendering regression: repeated per-glyph style and paint work was added to an interactive resize path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll a session transcript or use pointer input while the layered wallpaper is visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Captured scroll events schedule the interactive source renderer; it rescans the grid and confetti geometry, but unchanged dimensions leave cached opacity equal and perform no new style writes. Pointer movement adds no renderer work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The refresh scan scales with the same viewport grid, while effective style-write cardinality is zero for unchanged dimensions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Scroll bursts are coalesced by the source renderer's `RunOnceScheduler`; replicas are laid out by chat layout/resize rather than each pointer event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm cell maps are reused, and numeric opacity caching suppresses assignments on unchanged scroll refreshes. No negative-cache or lifecycle issue is present.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call path and zero style writes, supported by the added scroll test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The added `Math.hypot` per scanned cell has device-dependent CPU cost, but no evidence establishes user-visible degradation beyond the substantial pre-existing scan.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the added arithmetic is bounded and cached visual state avoids repaint on ordinary scrolling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show the Codicons setting under high-contrast themes or switch background presets
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The background service resolves the configured value and `setBackground` synchronously hides or clears renderer state; the changed production renderer does not introduce an external operation on this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Clearing scales with retained grid cells when leaving Codicons; this lifecycle existed before, with three retained layer nodes now cleared individually.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread update driven by one background-change event; no fan-out beyond existing source and replica renderers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cells are cleared when Codicons are disabled and rebuilt if re-enabled; no unbounded retention or stale cache was introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High after tracing service callers and `setBackground`/`clearCodicons`.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Theme/background switch frequency is low and no new scaling boundary is present.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: fixture/service changes validate suppression, and the production diff does not add expensive boundary work or unbounded state.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and every diff page. One resize-path rendering regression was submitted. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundaries are introduced or moved onto the affected product paths, and the PR does not provide evidence of fixing a prior shipped performance regression.
